journal.title: Candle patterns on large caps and daily candles (Vamsi's follow-up): still no edge worth trading
journal.body:
Same 13 patterns (scripts/candle_backtest.py), two more universes and timeframes.
Large caps, hourly (60 largest US stocks plus SPY and QQQ, 730 sessions; research/backtests/candles-2026-10-10-large.md): no pattern moves the next hour more than 0.05% from the baseline (+0.00%, 51% up). The +0.5%/-0.5% scalp: a third of trades reach the target first, a third the stop, a third neither; -0.00% before costs, -0.09% after; patterns -0.08% to +0.02% before costs.
Daily candles, 5 years (candles-daily-2026-10-10[-large].md): on large caps the hammer beat the baseline by +0.11% the next day and +0.34% over 5 days, bullish harami by +0.13% the next day, both positive in each half of the dates, but inside the noise (CIs ±0.13% and ±0.40%), and bearish engulfing also beat it over 5 days (+0.18%): the shared ingredient is a fall before the signal, not the shape. On the radar names the positive edges (morning star, big green bar, evening star, bearish engulfing) carry CIs of ±0.3% to ±2.7%, and two of them are bearish patterns followed by gains.
52 comparisons in the daily runs alone: two or three look good by chance at 95%. Verdict unchanged: no rule change; short-term reversal after a fall is the one effect, already traded by the night sleeve (RUNBOOK 2e).

journal.title: Hourly candle patterns tested (Vamsi's question): no pattern beats a random hour; a +0.5% scalp loses even before costs
journal.body:
Test (scripts/candle_backtest.py, research/backtests/candles-2026-10-10.md): 13 classic patterns (hammer, engulfing, piercing line, morning/evening star, harami, three white soldiers/black crows, shooting star, dark cloud cover, big green/red bars) on 63 radar candidates' hourly bars, 730 sessions (Nov 2023 to Oct 9), bought at the next hour's open; baseline: every hour of the same names.

Frequency: 0.9 to 12.9 signals a day across the names, so a pattern appears somewhere every day.
Next hour, before costs: baseline +0.00% (48% up). Bullish patterns -0.01% to -0.06% (46-49% up); bearish ones +0.01% to +0.11% (49-53% up). The largest effects (three black crows +0.10, big red bar +0.07, in both halves of the dates) point the opposite way to the textbook: a small bounce after weakness, no bigger than a round trip's cost (0.10% at $20+, 0.40% at $5-20).
The +0.5% scalp (5-minute bars, last 60 sessions): sold at +0.5% or stopped at -0.5%, the baseline reaches the target first 40% of the time and the stop 56%: -0.08% a trade before costs, -0.33% after. No bullish pattern improves it (30-42% target hits). Without a stop the target is hit 58-68% of the time, but the misses run to the close: -0.25% to -0.58% a trade after costs.
Scale: $2,000 needs +110% in 18 sessions, 4.2% of the account a session; +0.5% on a 25% position adds 0.125%, and even all-in 0.5% a day compounds to +9.4% by Nov 4.
Verdict: no rule change. The one effect present (buying weakness) is traded on the daily scale by the night sleeve (RUNBOOK 2e), where the move clears the costs.

journal.title: Strategy review Oct 8: what lost, 13 changes tested, paper rules unchanged
journal.body:
Vamsi asked for the strategies to evolve. What lost: the paper book's five closed trades this week were all stopped (POET, UMAC, CIFR, HUT, APLD), every one a high-beta name from one corner of the market (crypto miners, AI infrastructure, speculative tech), with stops about 0.6 ATR under the entry, inside a normal day's range. On Oct 8 that group fell together (25 of 67 names down 1+ ATR, bitcoin -3%), and supports do not hold in a group sell-off.

New lab (scripts/strategy_lab.py, 33 separate 22-session windows since Nov 2023): buy-and-hold of the eligible candidates averaged +7.7% a window, the radar under the live rules +4.5%: the radar's timing has added nothing to the names' own drift. Over 5 years the candidates' whole return came overnight (close to open +0.20% a night, open to close -0.02%), and a close 1.5+ ATR under the prior close rebounded +0.53% overnight after costs (58% up). Momentum rotation was far more volatile (worst window -51%). Nothing doubled $1,000 in any window.

Tested against the live rules on the RUNBOOK 2d test (mean and worst of the hourly windows, and the 5-minute windows): a breadth gate (no entries while the radar's median name is down 0.3-0.75 ATR), no entry on a stock-specific drop while SPY is up, entries only in the last half hour, stops 1.0-2.0 ATR under support sized on the stop, a trend switch (entries only while the candidates' index or QQQ is over its 10- or 20-day average), and selling half at +1 or +1.5 ATR. None beat the live paper rules on both tests; the trend switch lost 6-7% a window over the last 60 sessions. A night sleeve (2 slots, buy at 15:55 the names down 1.5+ ATR closing in the lowest quarter of the range, sell at the open) improved the hourly windows (mean +4.8% vs +4.5%, worst -19.2% vs -21.9%) but lost 0.4 points on the 5-minute windows, so the paper rules stay as they are.

journal.title: Oct 7 lessons tested: 1% gap allowance adopted, 9:45 entries and four other rules rejected
journal.body:
Vamsi asked (Wed Oct 7, about 10:30 AM) for the day's lessons to be evaluated and applied at once, without waiting for approval. Seven candidate rules came out of this morning's stops; each was replayed against the live rules before anything changed (research/backtests/lessons-2026-10-07.md; reports in research/replay/*-lessons.md and *-realbook.md). Adoption test (RUNBOOK 2d): beat the live rules on the mean and the worst window of the 33 separate hourly 22-session windows without losing on the 5-minute windows.

Adopted now:
- Size on the stop distance plus a 1% gap allowance (levels.GAP_PCT). Half the replay's stops gapped through at the open and filled on average 1.06% under their price. Hourly windows: mean +3.1% against +2.6%, worst -24.2% against -25.4%; 5-minute windows: mean +5.2% against +4.8%. levels.py check and orders.py plan print the new size (a stop 10% under the entry now gets 13.6% of equity instead of 15%).
- Mechanical fixes: pre-market moves are now measured from the last close (Yahoo's previousClose is two sessions back before the open: TEM showed -15.9% "pre-market" on a -2.2% night); a real-book position whose price is already under its stop is sold with a limit instead of a stop order the broker would reject.

Rejected after the test: entries only from 9:45 (worse in every real-book sample: support limits filled on gap-down opens often catch the low of the day); no entry within 0.3-0.45 ATR of its stop; no entry while down 1.0 or 1.5+ ATR on the day; selling a gapped stop at 9:55 instead of the open. Watch list: entries only 0.25+ ATR under the prior close (best over the last 60 sessions, mean +8.2% against +4.8% and 27 of 30 windows ahead of the S&P 500, but worse over 2.8 years: hourly-window mean +1.6% against +2.6%). The S&P gate stays out of the paper book (it cut the paper rules' returns in all four samples).

Self-review: the 9:45 rule was proposed from one trade and turned out to be the worst change tested. RUNBOOK 2a already says one trade changes nothing; this morning's proposals broke that rule and the replay caught it. Proposals now come with the test, not after it.

journal.title: Nearer targets: better in the last 60 sessions, worse over 2.8 years (replay, Oct 6)
journal.body:
Vamsi's point (Oct 6): the targets are too high; exit at the first target when the gain is meaningful and re-enter at the next support test. Tested in the replay (scripts/replay.py --set targets): the target is the lower of the sell-zone bottom and either the first resistance above the entry (any touches, 0.5+ ATR up) or entry + 1, 1.5, 2 or 3 ATR; re-entry after a target exit allowed as before.
- Last 30 sessions, 5-minute bars (research/replay/replay-2026-10-05-30-5m-targets.md): live +3.2% (17 trades, 18% winners); first resistance +4.1%, +1 ATR +3.9%, +1.5 ATR +4.7%, +2 ATR +5.6% (32% winners, profit factor 1.3), +3 ATR -0.1%.
- 5-minute windows (8 overlapping 22-session windows of the last 60 sessions; windows-2026-10-05-22-5m-targets.md): live mean +4.9%, worst -5.2%; +2 ATR +6.0% and -3.4%; first resistance +5.3% and -4.2%.
- 33 separate 22-session windows over 2.8 years, hourly bars (windows-2026-10-05-22-1h-targets.md): live median +4.8%, mean +3.4%, worst -20.9%, best +41.5%. First resistance mean +0.7%; +1 ATR -0.1% (best window only +13.9%); +1.5 ATR +2.7% (worst -18.8%); +2 ATR +1.7%; +3 ATR +3.1% (worst -18.3%, best +43.3%).
Verdict: no change (the 2d gate needs a better mean and worst window on the 2.8 years). Nearer targets helped in the recent choppy months, but over 2.8 years the trades that ran to the far targets paid for the stops; capping them at +1 ATR cut the best window from +41.5% to +13.9%. Closest alternative: +3 ATR (mean 3.1% against 3.4%, worst window -18.3% against -20.9%), a draw rather than a gain. Re-run at the Sunday replay as more choppy sessions come in.

journal.title: Protecting open gains: break-even and trailing stops lose to holding for the target (replay, Oct 6)
journal.body:
Vamsi's point (Oct 6, after the book slipped from +4.9% at 9:55 to +2.25% at 10:44): plan the exits so the book doesn't give back its gains. Tested in the replay (scripts/replay.py --set exits): once a position's best price is 0.5-1.5 ATR over the entry, its stop rises to the entry (break-even) or trails 0.5-1.5 ATR under the best price.
- Last 30 sessions, 5-minute bars (research/replay/replay-2026-10-05-30-5m-exits.md): live rules +3.2%; tight trails did better (0.75 ATR after +0.5: +6.6%; 0.5 ATR after +1: +5.8%), a 1-ATR trail worse (-3.5%), break-even stops +2.8% and +0.6%.
- 33 separate 22-session windows over 2.8 years, hourly bars (windows-2026-10-05-22-1h-exits.md): live rules median +4.8%, mean +3.4%, worst -20.9%. Every variant had a lower mean (+0.8% to +2.8%); break-even after +0.5 ATR had the best worst window (-18.4%) but a mean of +2.8% and a median of +1.2%; the tight trails that led over 30 sessions fell to means of +0.8% and +2.0%.
- 5-minute windows (8 overlapping, windows-2026-10-05-22-5m-exits.md): live mean +4.9%, every variant lower (-0.5% to +3.9%).
Verdict: no change (the 2d gate needs a better mean and worst window). With 18-33% of trades winning, the targets pay for the stops; stops raised on open gains sell the winners early, on these stocks' normal 5-7% daily swings, and the trades they free up do worse. Today's give-back was open profit moving with the stocks; no position came near its stop or target.

journal.title: Dip recovery times and channel quality (tests, Oct 6)
journal.body:
Vamsi's questions (Oct 6): how many days do dips take to recover and how much comes back; and is proper channel trading (buy the bottom, sell the top) better?
Recovery (scripts/dip_recovery.py; research/backtests/dip-recovery-2026-10-06.md; 3,066 closes 1+ ATR under the prior close, median drop -8.7%, 4 years): back at the pre-dip close 6% of the time the next day, 31% within 5 sessions, 46% within 10, 60% within 20. Half the drop came back in a median 3 sessions (73% got there within 20). By the 10th session the median dip had won back only 11% of its drop, and the next 5 sessions' lows went a median 6.2% under the dip's close first. Dips of 2-3 ATR won back 34% by day 10; 3+ ATR crashes (median -19%) 0%, with 18% back within 10 sessions. Offering dips: 30% back within 10 sessions, a further 9.7% lower first, and the median drop grew (-23% of it by day 10). For PCVX (an offering dip from 73.82) those base rates say: about 30% odds of seeing 73.82 again within 10 sessions and 42% within 20, with a typical further fall of about 10% first, to around 59 (the 57.30-59.70 support zone).
Channels (scripts/channel_backtest.py; research/backtests/channels-2026-10-06.md; 2,959 radar touch trades over 5 years, 10-session time exit): all trades 33% winners, target hit 23%, stopped 63%, average -0.003R, the same as random entries with the same stop and target. Proper channels (support and resistance tested 3+ times each) +0.26% a trade, -0.034R against random -0.046R; 4+ touches each +0.025R against +0.010R; channels 5+ ATR wide worse (-0.159R, target hit 3%). The number of touches does not make the bottom of a channel a better entry.
Verdict: no switch to channel trading (the radar already is one, and channel quality made no difference). What the tests support: skip offering dips, skip dips while the whole market falls (to replay), expect the price to go about 6% lower before a dip recovers, and give recoveries days, not hours.

journal.title: Intraday dips of 3-10%: rarely back by the close; pay over days, not hours; skip market-wide down days (test, Oct 6)
journal.body:
Vamsi's point (Oct 6): a dip is a fall of 3-4% or more at any time of the session, often recovered by the close, invisible on daily bars. Test (scripts/intraday_dip_backtest.py; research/backtests/intraday-dips-2026-10-06.md): 61 radar candidates, hourly bars, ~2 years, 39,536 sessions; a buy limit X% under the open fills when the price trades through it; no stop.
- Frequency: a 4% dip under the open happens in 32% of sessions for these names (3%: 44%, 5%: 23%, 10%: 5%).
- Same day: the dip rarely closes back at the open (12% for 4% dips, 3% for 10% dips). From the fill to the close: -0.58% for 4% dips, -0.44% for 10% (buying every open: -0.34%).
- Over 3 sessions: +0.50% for 4% dips, +0.79% for 7%, +1.20% (95% range +/-1.44) for 10%; buying any open +0.46%. Deeper dips lean better; only 10% dips under the prior close stand out a little (+0.24% to the close, 52% up, +1.42% over 3 sessions).
- Market-wide down days (SPY down 1%+): 4% dips lost 2.59% by the close (22% up) and 1.51% by the next close. On other days: -0.20% to the close, +0.76% over 3 sessions.
- No difference with or without company news (+0.27% and +0.58% over 3 sessions), or inside the support band or not (+0.63%, +0.56%). Dips filled after 12:30 did best over 3 sessions (+1.13%) against the first hour (+0.31%).
Verdict: the dip that closes back where it started is the exception, not the pattern; buying intraday dips earns over days, about as much as buying any open, except that dips on a falling market keep falling. Candidate rule for the Sunday replay (2d): no paper dip buys while SPY is down 1%+ on the day (the real book already stops new orders at -0.35%).

journal.title: Dips with and without company news: offerings keep falling, other dips recover (test, Oct 6)
journal.body:
Vamsi's question (J0022): do dips without a fundamental reason recover, and dips with one not? Test (scripts/news_dip_backtest.py; research/backtests/news-dips-2026-10-06.md): 66 radar candidates, last 4 years, 3,127 sessions that closed 1+ ATR under the prior close; company news = an SEC filing (8-K, 6-K, offering, 10-Q/10-K) from the day before to the day after. Returns after slippage, 95% ranges clustered by date; baseline +0.24% over 3 sessions from any close.
- All dips: +0.65% after 3 sessions (49% up), +1.65% after 5. A small recovery effect, a coin flip trade by trade.
- No company news: +0.68% (3 sessions). Company news: +0.58%. No difference overall.
- By kind of news: offerings and registrations -1.07% (42% up; buying the next open -1.92%); results +1.37% (+2.51% after 5 sessions); other 8-Ks +0.66%. The fundamental dip that keeps falling is dilution; earnings dips recovered at least as well as dips with no news.
- Support: no-news dips whose low reached the radar support +1.18% after 3 sessions (+2.16% after 5) against +0.44% for the rest.
- Market-wide (SPY down 1%+) against stock-specific no-news dips: +0.90% and +0.55%, no clear difference. Dips of 2+ ATR: +1.54% without news, +1.09% with (wide ranges).
- Waiting for an up close before buying: no gain on no-news dips (+0.41% against +0.68% at the dip's close); on news dips +1.61% against +0.58%, mostly by skipping offering dips that kept falling.
Verdict: half of the idea holds. The cause that matters is dilution (already a skip in 2a), and buying at support adds about 0.7 points over 3 sessions (2a already buys only there). A blanket no-news filter would have skipped the earnings dips that recovered best. No rule change: none of these beat the live rules in the 2d replay yet. Caveat: SEC filings are a crude record of a dip's cause (analyst notes, peer results and sector news file nothing).

journal.title: Focus: big dips with no fundamental reason, bought where they reverse (Vamsi, Oct 6)
journal.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Tue Oct 6, 10:00 AM): the paper book's gain came from dip recoveries, so focus on big dips. For each one, first find why it fell: company news that changes the business (offering, guidance cut, failed trial, legal or regulatory hit) or market and sector emotion with no company reason. Skip the first kind; for the second, find the support where it is likely to reverse and buy the reversal.
Check against the book so far: POET, HUT and CIFR, bought at 9:56 Mon Oct 5 while 2.9-4.1% (about 0.5 ATR) under their prior closes with no company news, made $45.35 of the $49.32 gain by 9:55 Tue; UMAC, bought without a dip, made $3.98. How it maps onto the rules: entries already go deepest dip first at support (2a, Oct 5), and company news that changes the business already cancels an entry. What is new is making the dip's cause the first question and waiting for the reversal. Test first (RUNBOOK 2d): scripts/news_dip_backtest.py compares dips with and without company news (SEC filings), at support or not, market-wide or not, buying the dip's close, the next open, or after a confirming up close. Results and any rule change follow in a research entry.

journal.title: Replay practice: the rules over the last 30 sessions and 2.8 years, as if live (Vamsi, Oct 5)
journal.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Mon Oct 5, night): practice the rules on the last 30 trading days as if live, without looking at what happened next, and learn from the bad cases.
Built scripts/replay.py. Each session uses only what was known then: the radar from the prior closes, the 8:40 resting limits, the bitcoin gate at 8:40, fills and stops bar by bar, targets and dip-first buys at the runs, T+1 settlement. No news filter. Reports in research/replay/.
Last 30 sessions (Aug 24-Oct 5, 5-minute bars), $1,000 under the Oct 6 rules: -6.4% (S&P 500 +1.2%, Nasdaq-100 +6.0%). 14 closed trades: 13 stopped, 1 target. 17 of 40 resting orders filled.
The bad cases:
- Support limits filled while the price fell through support: 9 of 14 never rose 0.5 ATR above the entry; 4 were stopped the session they were bought (RXRX and SMCI within 15 minutes of the Aug 24 open).
- 4 gapped through the stop overnight and sold at the open below it (-3.4% to -5.1%). RCAT, RGTI and SMR went together on Sep 10: three speculative small-caps, one bet.
- GPUS lost 9.1% and 10.2% (Sep 1 and 2) at full size: its stop sat about 9-10% under the entry, so a 25% position risked 2.3-2.5% of equity.
- GPUS, Aug 25: after a 6-session trading halt (Aug 17-24) the radar's "support" was the flat 0.45 halt print; the limit filled at the reopen and the stock fell 19% in 5 minutes.
- The one winner, RKLB (+21.6%), was bought at the open on a 0.83-ATR gap down and held 8 sessions to its target.
Over 2.8 years (hourly bars, 33 separate 22-session windows) the same rules made a median +4.8% (mean +1.9%), from -30% to +28%, and beat the S&P 500 in 17 of 33. None of the 25 variants tested doubled $1,000 in any 22-session window; the best 30-session window of any variant was +123%.
Trade by trade over 2.8 years (368 trades): +1.44% a trade (+/- 2.0), 19% winners averaging +32%, losers -5.8%. The rules make money only through rare targets. First-hour entries averaged +2.8% and entries after 10:30 -1.8% (+/- 2.2), yet stopping entries at 10:30 did not improve the windows; every other split (dip depth, gap, market direction, support strength, R:R) sat inside the noise.
Variants (research/replay/): limits at the zone top, run entries only, a 3-session time exit, stops 0.8-1.5 ATR, no bitcoin gate, R:R ranking, opening gap-down day trades, a 10:00 limit cancel, entry-time cutoffs, tested support for GPUS/IREN/BTDR, risk-based sizing. Results swing with the start date: the best of 15 variants on the last 60 sessions showed a +7.8% median and was ordinary over 2.8 years. Worse in every test: the 3-session exit. Worse in most: limits at the zone top. No bitcoin gate: worse over 2.8 years, better in the last 60 sessions.

journal.title: Resting buys move to support, the bottom of the buy zone; bitcoin gate for crypto-linked names (Vamsi, Oct 5)
journal.body:
Vamsi's instruction (Mon Oct 5, night): put the resting buy at the bottom of the buy zone, so a deep dip in the first 30 minutes fills it automatically; prepare the buy levels for every radar name; buy only with confidence, good R:R and a good dip; and don't chase dips in crypto-linked stocks without checking bitcoin's sentiment.
Applied from Tue Oct 6: paper buy limits sit at support (the bottom of the zone), R:R measured from support (1.5+), names within 8% of support, higher R:R first. A bitcoin gate decides crypto-linked entries: open while bitcoin is above its 20-day average, down less than 2% on the day and less than 5% over 3 days (tonight: open, 85,302 against 82,858). The radar check already holds the buy level, stop and sell zone for every name; the broker-side limit order does the watching between runs.
Tested (research/backtests/limits-2026-10-06.md, 2 years of hourly bars): a limit at support fills 42% of the time against 63% at the zone top, and fills on deeper dips that often keep falling: the 0.6-ATR stop was hit within 3 sessions 62% of the time (49% from the zone top). Average result 3 sessions later: -0.12% from support, -0.04% from the zone top; with the stop 1.0 or 1.5 ATR under support, +0.08% and +0.21%, with 39% and 20% stopped out. All inside the noise: the bottom of the zone is a different trade-off (cheaper entries, fewer fills, more stop-outs), not a better trade.
